author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Untrusted `page` request parameter is clamped at the controller boundary (OwnerController.processFindForm -> firstPageWhenBelowStart) before any use, matching docs/security-principles.md 'Validate at the boundary'; the clamp is total over int (Math.max(requestedPage, 1)), so Integer.MIN_VALUE cannot underflow the later `page - 1` in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName.

No new attack surface: no new endpoint, parameter, dependency, file/resource path, deserialization, reflection, or binder change. build.gradle is untouched, so the supply-chain check is a no-op for this diff (no version, coordinate, or repository change to verify against NVD).

Data access is unchanged and still a Spring Data derived query (findByLastNameStartingWith) with a Pageable — no string-concatenated SQL, so the clamped value reaches persistence only as a bound parameter.

Upper bound on the same parameter is not a security defect here: page=2147483647 yields PageRequest.of(2147483646, 5) with a long offset (no overflow), an empty result, and the existing 'not found' branch rendering owners/findOwners with HTTP 200 — no exception, no stack trace, no unbounded row read (page size fixed at 5). Non-numeric input still fails Spring type conversion at binding, before the handler body, which is pre-existing behavior the diff does not alter.

No XSS or template-injection exposure introduced: `currentPage` is an int, and the Thymeleaf preprocessing forms in owners/ownersList.html (`__${currentPage - 1}__`, `__${currentPage + 1}__`) inline a numeric value, never request-derived text. Default output escaping is untouched.

Net reduction in exposure: `/owners?page=0` previously reached the error page, which renders the underlying exception message (docs/security-principles.md, secret-disclosure row); the clamp removes that error-page path for below-range pages.
No hardcoded credential, token, key, or other secret in either changed file; the test fixture uses existing in-suite owner data only.

Class sweep for the finding class 'unclamped request-parameter value reaching a range-checked API' across the change set found no further instance in the diff. VetController's identical `page` parameter is pre-existing surface outside this change set and is not made weaker by it.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage drives two boundary values ("0", "-1") through a `for` loop inside the test body. testing-principles.md § Assertions states 'No branching in assertions | No if/else, switch, or loops' and § Test Naming's parameterized-test row says repetitive cases stay data-driven via a table or CSV source. This is a newly written test (post-2026-07-31), so the grandfather clause for pre-existing tests does not cover it, and other loop-bodied tests already in the file (e.g. processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace) are pre-existing debt out of this diff's scope, not precedent to follow.
findings.fix: Convert to @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource(value = {"0", "-1"}) (or a 'requestedPage,expectedPage' two-column source) supplying the below-first-page values, keeping the single method name per the brief's parameterized-test convention.

findings.description: The new test copies `Page<Owner> tasks = new PageImpl<>(...)` verbatim from processFindFormSuccess directly above it. 'tasks' does not describe the value's role (a two-owner results page used only to drive pagination through the controller) and the three-tier naming convention calls for a role name or a SOME_/ANY_-prefixed anonymous factory for irrelevant test data written from 2026-07-31 onward.
findings.fix: Rename to a role-describing local, e.g. `twoOwnersPage`, or route through an anonymous factory (e.g. `createAPageOfOwners(2)`) per testing-principles.md § Anonymous Factories.

approved_aspects: theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage genuinely pins the reported defect: pre-fix, page=0/-1 flow into PageRequest.of(page-1, size) with a negative index, which PageRequest rejects by throwing IllegalArgumentException before the controller ever reaches status().isOk() — the test fails against the old code and passes only once firstPageWhenBelowStart clamps the value, so it is a real regression guard rather than a tautology.
Test name follows the brief's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school.
Both documented boundary values from the bug report (page=0 and page=-1) are exercised, and the model assertion (currentPage == 1) verifies the actual clamped output rather than just a 200 status.
./gradlew test passes with the new test included; no regressions introduced elsewhere in OwnerControllerTests.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owners page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: Three files, seven hunks, no sensitive paths: one controller method plus its private helper, one new test, and three doc lines in CLAUDE.md. The prod edit is confined to OwnerController.processFindForm and changes nothing outside the /owners request path.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk; the clamp is a pure Math.max at the binding boundary and behaviour for page >= 1 is bit-identical, with no upper bound, no change to the lastName strip path, and no change to the single-owner redirect. The one real trap the rename set - losing the query-parameter binding when the parameter became requestedPage - is closed explicitly by @RequestParam(name = "page").

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test drives page=0 and page=-1 through the real MockMvc request path and would fail against the unfixed code, since PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws rather than returning 200. Asserting currentPage == 1 covers the second half of the fix, the pagination model. Minor slack: the any(Pageable.class) stub never pins that the repository actually received page index 0.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved, but doc-reviewer's approval carries an escalate-tagged finding: scripts/layout.toml:123 still declares the gate command as './gradlew build && ./gradlew test && ./gradlew checkJavaFormat', a task this build does not define, so the declared gate command is broken as written. Verified in the file. It is correctly routed rather than unresolved - the file is the plugin's regenerated engine sliver and the stale name originates upstream in the plugin-owned code-quality-gate skill - but an approval carrying an escalate tag is a hedge by definition and this one names a live tooling residual.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries; the slice never fought its triage. The CLAUDE.md correction is a rider on a pagination bugfix, but it is three lines of stale Gradle task names, reviewer-requested, and separately recorded in .scratch/escalations.md.

rationale: Pagination fix is clean and the test genuinely fails against the old code. Two residuals deserve a look before merging: the escalated scripts/layout.toml:123 gate command still names the nonexistent checkJavaFormat task and needs an upstream plugin fix, and VetController keeps the identical unclamped PageRequest.of(page - 1).
